catalog: LedgerLock reference fixture — mutants (WP-2.0.3). One mutant, one exact source change, one target requirement. `before` is a line of reference/ledgerlock/<module> that occurs exactly once; `after` replaces it (null deletes it). `expect_fail` names the assertions that must fail; `consequential` names assertions that the same defect necessarily reaches (declared, never a second target); any other failure invalidates the mutant.

mutants.consequence: keys are normalised to NFD instead of NFC: the spellings still meet, but the stored and snapshotted key is not the NFC form the requirement fixes; every snapshot keyed by an NFC non-ASCII key shows the NFD form
every hash is computed without the '|' separator; the chain is self-consistent but not the specified one, so only an independent recomputation sees it

mutants.before: prev = records[-1]["hash"] if records else GENESIS
mutants.consequence: append never chains: every line's prev_hash is GENESIS; verify (which recomputes linkage) rejects any chain of two or more appended lines, so every observation that verifies a multi-line chain or repairs one sees it

verify never recomputes a hash: a mutated value, op or hash field passes; corruption anywhere in a well-linked chain is invisible, so repair-tail no longer refuses mid-chain corruption and the CLI never exits 5 for it

verify never checks that prev_hash equals the previous line's hash: a changed prev_hash field goes unnoticed (a removed line is still caught by the hash recomputation, whose input is the previous line's hash)
first_bad_index is one too high; repair-tail, which compares it with the last index, refuses a genuinely truncated tail

mutants.after: return verify_raw(raw) if self._known_length is None else Verdict(True, None, self._known_length)
mutants.consequence: after this instance appended, verify answers from what it remembers instead of the disk

mutants.before: if not isinstance(rid, str) or rid == "":
mutants.consequence: an empty rid is accepted and a line is written with it

mutants.after: if rid in seen and seen[rid][1]["key"] != key:
mutants.consequence: a replayed rid on the same key is treated as new and appends again; every replay-based no-op (tombstone replay, NFC replay, in-batch replay, replay after a refused delete) appends instead

mutants.before: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] != rid:
mutants.after: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] == rid:
mutants.consequence: the conflict condition is inverted and can never hold after the replay check, so no mutation conflicts: tombstones and different-op mutations are accepted, batches with a conflict commit, and the CLI never exits 4

mutants.before: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] != rid:
mutants.after: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] != rid and last_rec["op"] == "put":
mutants.consequence: only a live value conflicts; a tombstone no longer blocks a different rid

mutants.before: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] != rid:
mutants.after: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] != rid and last_rec["op"] == op:
mutants.consequence: a different rid conflicts only when it repeats the last op: delete-after-put and put-after-tombstone with a different rid are accepted

mutants.before: raise ConflictError(f"batch op {len(results)}: key {normalize_key(key)!r} was last mutated by another rid")
mutants.consequence: a conflict inside a batch ends the batch instead of refusing it: the ops before the conflict are committed (a partial batch) and the CLI exits 0
a rid first seen inside the batch is not remembered, so its replay later in the same batch appends a second line
the snapshot lists keys in insertion order, not UTF-8 byte order
a tombstoned key stays in the snapshot; every snapshot that must exclude a deleted key shows it
the clean-chain no-op never applies: repair-tail on an intact chain removes its last line
repair-tail no longer requires the first violation to be the last line: an unterminated file with mid-chain corruption is 'repaired' by dropping its tail instead of refused
repair-tail removes two lines instead of the truncated one
an append returns before its bytes are durable: no fsync in the append path
a conflict exits 5 instead of 4; every CLI observation of a conflict sees the wrong code
an I/O error exits 1 instead of 3

mutants.before: return EXIT_OK if verdict.ok else EXIT_CORRUPT
mutants.consequence: verify exits 0 whatever the verdict (the verdict on stdout is still correct)
